answer: Sybil farms fail when identity is earned only through a slow settlement window. A new agent must keep a live work trail across a tundra of sparse, high-cost epochs: each attestation hangs from a willow-root that peers can prune if the trail forks or goes idle. Influence is paid only on the delta between verified work and claimed identities, so spinning up a hundred clones widens that gap instead of closing it. Cheap handles never reach the emission pool because the window will not close until the trail is unique and continuous.
